claims.text: The rider's record may not be used to build the case against her. Her 3 prior_no_show_flags is a LIFETIME counter and is not the rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d that POL-NS-09(d) reads; the trailing-30-day figure on this profile is 1, far below the threshold of 3, so no abuse escalation arises out of her side of the file. Under POL-GEN-01 her rating (4.66), account_age_days (1830), lifetime_trips (1290), cancellation_rate (0.071), prior_disputes_filed (4) and prior_disputes_upheld (1) are CONTEXT ONLY: they may inform how closely her assertions are scrutinised and may never ground or carry an adverse finding about this trip. The only rider field citable on a no-show question is no_show_disputes_30d, and it does not support a finding against her.

I do not put POL-NS-04, and I say so rather than stretch it. The rider did send a coordinating message inside the waiting window ('coming coming 2 min', sent 16:08:02, read 16:08:11), but limb (b) fails on the driver's side of the record: he replied 'ok no problem' at 16:08:20, eighteen seconds later, and placed an in-app call that was answered for 34 seconds at 16:09:40, both before he terminated the trip. Limb (c) fails on the rider's own track, which records 0 qualifying fixes inside the 150 m rider_presence_radius_m for this LARGE_VENUE zone. On this record the rider-contact clause cannot be made out.

The thing this record does not settle is where the rider was, and the two admissible artifacts that speak to it contradict each other directly. The chat log shows the rider telling the driver at 16:08:02 that she is 'coming coming 2 min' - an assertion that she was moving and moments away - while the rider's own track in the same window records 141 fixes from 15:54:00 to 16:15:20 at a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph and a mean distance of 639.8 m from the pickup pin: on the platform's own telemetry she never moved at all. No clause resolves which of the two is right; POL-NS-04(c) can only say she was outside the 150 m presence radius on admissible fixes, not whether she was on her way. I do not dispute that the driver's own hold of the guardhouse ran 585 seconds inside the arrival radius - my point is that the rider's side of the same event is unresolved on admissible artifacts, which is the POL-NS-09(b) situation of two artifacts in direct conflict on rider presence with no clause to settle it. That is also exactly what the rider asked for: somebody to call her about this. Escalated, the disputed $8.00 is held rather than collected under POL-GEN-03, which is the only outcome on this record that does not charge the rider on a question the platform cannot answer.

The rider never named a block, tower, bay or entrance: her only message in the window is 'coming coming 2 min', and POL-NS-03 is the clause that deals with a rider who is not at the labelled point but is not to blame for it - where neither party specified a sub-location and registered_pickup_points is 2 or more, it attributes the mislocation to pin ambiguity rather than to either party, and the platform-funded goodwill is never recovered from the rider. The trip record's own figures show a condominium pickup with 2 registered pickup points and a pin labelled 'Main Guardhouse', while the rider's track sits 633.9 to 646.4 m from that pin for the entire window. I accept that POL-NS-03's 120-to-400 m distance gate cannot itself be run here, because the driver's fixes fall inside the 120 m arrival radius, so the clause does not by its own terms produce the refund; I ask the Judge to record the pin ambiguity as the specific open question the reviewer must settle under POL-NS-09, because treating a 640 m gap between the platform's own pin and the platform's own rider track as the rider's fault is not something this record supports.

The trip record for TRP-00208 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 16:02:25 and shows the trip terminated by the driver at 16:12:10 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event anywhere in the record, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are satisfied on the platform's own telemetry.

EV-GPS-00208 is an unbroken 10-second trace at 100 percent coverage with zero gaps, and it places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius on 60 qualifying fixes, the first of them at 16:02:10 — fifteen seconds before the 16:02:25 arrived event — so the POL-NS-02 proximity test and POL-NS-01 limb (b) are met.

The driver held position inside the pickup geofence in a single unbroken run of 585 seconds, from 16:02:10 to 16:11:55, against a LARGE_VENUE minimum dwell of 300 seconds — a surplus of 285 seconds — so POL-NS-01 limb (c) is met, and met on one continuous qualifying run rather than by any accumulation.

The arrival marker is not a false marker under POL-NS-05: the 16:02:25 arrived event falls inside the same continuous in-geofence run that begins at 16:02:10, the driver's recorded speeds include 0.0 km/h, and nothing in the trace puts him more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or above at the moment he marked arrival.

POL-NS-03 cannot apply on this record. Its 400 m wrong-entrance test is confined to a driver stationary OUTSIDE the POL-NS-02 arrival radius; the driver here was stationary inside the 120 m radius for the whole qualifying run, at his closest 28.8 m from the recorded pickup pin at 'The Interlace, Main Guardhouse, 180 Depot Rd'. This is not a wrong-face-of-the-venue case at all.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. Her only coordinating message — 'coming coming 2 min' at 16:08:02 — was answered by the driver eighteen seconds later at 16:08:20 ('ok no problem'), and the driver placed an in-app voice call at 16:09:40 that was answered and ran 34 seconds, so limb (b) fails outright; and limb (c) fails affirmatively, because 0 of the rider's 141 fixes fall inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius.

The rider's account that she waited at her condo guardhouse for almost fifteen minutes is contradicted by her own device: all 141 rider fixes between 15:54:00 and 16:15:20 are stationary at 0.0 km/h, at a mean of 639.8 m from the pickup pin and never nearer than 633.9 m. She never left the Block 5 lift lobby roughly 640 m inside the estate and never came within the 150 m presence radius, so the failure to board was hers.

The rider's assertion that she 'call him also cannot get through' is contradicted by the chat log: it holds a driver-placed in-app voice call at 16:09:40 recorded as answered with a duration of 34 seconds, and delivery-and-read receipts showing she read the driver's 16:02:40 message with his plate 'SJK8842P' at 16:03:01 and his 16:07:15 follow-up at 16:07:29. Every message the driver sent was delivered and read.

The POL-NS-06 shortfall rule is not engaged. The effective in-geofence dwell is 585 seconds against a 300 second minimum, and the computed shortfall is minus 285 seconds, that is a surplus. The limb (i) accumulation route is unavailable in any event — EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING, its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, its weight is 0.0, and no advisory covers Depot Road in this window — and a MISSING advisory can never be asserted to excuse a shortfall. None is needed here.

The $8.00 charged reconciles with the fee schedule. Under the resolution rule the chargeable fee is the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee ($8.00), and the $8.00 cancellation-fee line is that vehicle-tier figure, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. Nor do limbs (a) to (c) bite: the arrived event sits 15 seconds from the nearest fix, the trace has no gap longer than 120 seconds and 120 fixes across the window, and the chat log holds 6 messages matching the record's chat_message_count of 6 with an unbroken msg_id sequence.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, the driver is entitled to compensation of 80 percent of the $8.00 fee, that is $6.40, and the anti-farming check does not withhold it: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 143 is 0.014, far below the 0.08 ratio. The rider's charge stands and the driver is paid.

No POL-NS-09 trigger fires. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the limb (d) threshold of 3, and her lifetime prior_no_show_flags of 3 is a different counter which under POL-GEN-01 is context only and may not be substituted for it. Both disputes_with_counterparty_90d fields are 0, so limb (c) is not met. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact in this bundle is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 — including the trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown — so limbs (a) and (e) are not engaged and no monetary ruling need be displaced by an escalation.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the $8.00 no-show fee on TRP-00208 was correctly charged and it stands; the driver is paid, out of it, $6.40. To the driver: your compensation is confirmed at 80 percent of the $8.00 fee, i.e. $6.40. The ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION because that is the outcome this case produces; the disposition of the fee itself is that your $8.00 charge is left in place. Under POL-GEN-03, where the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, amount_sgd carries the same figure as the driver payment.

Why the charge stands. POL-NS-01 needs four conditions and all four hold on this record. (a) The trip record (EV-TRIP-00208, weight 1.0) carries a driver 'arrived' event at 16:02:25. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00208, weight 1.0) — unbroken 10-second telemetry, 100 percent coverage, zero gaps — places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius from 16:02:10, fifteen seconds before the marker, on 60 qualifying fixes, closest approach 28.8 m from the pin. (c) The driver then held position inside that radius in one continuous run from 16:02:10 to 16:11:55: 585 seconds against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, a surplus of 285 seconds, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix as the clause requires. (d) The record shows no boarding and a driver termination at 16:12:10 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell elapsed at about 16:07:10. No clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces this.

Rider's claims, answered. POL-NS-02: the proximity test is satisfied because qualifying in-radius fixes exist, so it yields to the dwell finding rather than to a full refund. POL-NS-03 (pin ambiguity): the clause is not engaged and produces no goodwill. Its 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling applies only to a driver stationary OUTSIDE the arrival radius; this driver was stationary INSIDE the 120 m radius, at 28.8 m from the pin, so the clause's own gate cannot be run. The $4.00 pin-ambiguity goodwill is therefore not payable. POL-NS-04 (rider contact unanswered): the clause cannot be made out — limb (b) fails because the driver replied 'ok no problem' 18 seconds after the rider's 16:08:02 message and placed an in-app call at 16:09:40 that was answered for 34 seconds, and limb (c) fails because 0 of the rider's 141 fixes fall inside the 150 m presence radius. POL-NS-06: not engaged; effective dwell of 585 seconds against a 300-second minimum is a surplus of 285 seconds, not a shortfall, and the accumulation route is unnecessary and in any event unavailable because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0.

The rider's escalation argument (POL-NS-09(b)) is rejected. The rider's account that she waited at the guardhouse for almost fifteen minutes is contradicted by her own device, and her 'coming coming 2 min' message is contradicted by her track, which records 141 fixes stationary at 0.0 km/h, mean 639.8 m from the pin. But rider presence is not a deciding fact on this dispute: POL-NS-01 turns on the driver's arrival and dwell alone, and POL-NS-06 states a shortfall refund would apply 'whether or not the rider was present'. The clause that reads rider position, POL-NS-04(c), resolves presence from the track and excludes any inference that she was elsewhere. There is accordingly no unresolved clash on arrival, dwell or rider presence that the outcome depends on, and no terminal escalation.

Driver compensation. Under POL-NS-07 the driver receives 80 percent of the $8.00 fee, i.e. $6.40, the platform retaining 20 percent. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 143 is 0.014, below the 0.08 ratio. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor read from this policy; both disputes_with_counterparty_90d fields are 0; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the threshold of 3; no sole impaired artifact carries the deciding fact, and every artifact carrying a deciding fact (trip record, GPS trace, chat log, fare breakdown) is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so confidence is not discounted. The rider's prior_no_show_flags of 3 is a lifetime counter and, with her rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate and prior dispute counts, is context only under POL-GEN-01 and was used for no finding here.

Fare integrity. The $8.00 charged reconciles with the fee schedule: the resolution rule sets the fee at the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee ($8.00), and the vehicle-tier figure of $8.00 governs and is the line itemised. POL-NS-08(d) is therefore not engaged.

Referrals: none. POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival referral does not fire because the arrival marker was true — it falls inside the continuous in-geofence run and nothing puts the driver more than 300 m from the pin or in motion at 15 km/h or above when he marked arrival. No clause produces any other referral, and any open question about the rider's unexplained 640 m position gap is not one a clause directs into a referral.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the $8.00 the rider was charged is not refunded, and the driver is paid $6.40 compensation. The ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION.

The platform's own telemetry settles this. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00208) shows the driver's 'arrived' marker at 16:02:25 and the trip terminated by the driver at 16:12:10 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) hold. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00208) is complete 10-second telemetry at 100% coverage with no gaps: it puts the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius from 16:02:10 and holds him there in one continuous in-geofence run of 585 seconds to 16:11:55 — 285 seconds more than the 300-second minimum — so limbs (b) and (c) hold as well. He is not caught by the false-arrival rule (POL-NS-05): he was stationary inside the radius when he marked arrival, not more than 300 m away and not travelling at 15 km/h or above.

What the driver did to reach the rider is on the record: he messaged at 16:02:40 with his plate and again at 16:07:15, both marked read; the rider replied 'coming coming 2 min' at 16:08:02; he answered 'ok no problem' 18 seconds later and placed an in-app call at 16:09:40 that was answered and ran 34 seconds. That defeats the rider-contact clause POL-NS-04 — limb (b) fails because he replied within 120 seconds and called before terminating, and limb (c) fails because the rider's device, across 141 fixes between 15:54:00 and 16:15:20, is stationary at 0.0 km/h at a mean 639.8 m from the pin and never nearer than 633.9 m, i.e. never inside the 150 m rider-presence radius. The rider's account that she waited at the guardhouse and could not get through by phone is contradicted by her own device and by the answered call in the log.

Rider's arguments, answered. (1) The claimed contradiction between the chat log and the GPS rider track does not engage POL-NS-09(b): the chat log records what the rider said, not a second measurement of where she was, and POL-NS-04(c) is the clause that tests rider presence on admissible fixes — this is not two admissible artifacts in direct conflict on a fact no clause resolves. (2) POL-NS-06 is not engaged: the dwell exceeds the minimum by 285 seconds, and the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00208-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) is irrelevant because no accumulation across intervals is needed. (3) POL-NS-03 cannot run: its 400 m wrong-entrance test applies to a driver stationary OUTSIDE the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m, and this driver was stationary inside the 120 m radius, so the clause does not reach its distance gate and its pin-ambiguity goodwill is not payable. ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: I have decided this on the platform's own records for TRP-00208, and they agree with one another.

The driver's side is established. The GPS trace runs unbroken at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gap, and it places the driver at the main guardhouse inside the 120 m arrival radius for this condominium (LARGE_VENUE) pickup from 16:02:10, holding position in a single continuous run of 585 seconds until 16:11:55. The trip record carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 16:02:25 and the driver's cancellation at 16:12:10 on reason RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event. That satisfies all four conditions for a chargeable no-show: the arrival event exists; the trace puts the driver in the geofence before it (first qualifying fix 16:02:10, fifteen seconds before the marker); he held the geofence for at least the 300 seconds this zone class requires — he held it for 585 seconds, a surplus of 285 seconds; and the trip was terminated by the driver on the no-show code after the dwell had elapsed. The arrival marker is not false: the 16:02:25 event sits inside the same in-geofence run, with recorded speed 0.0 km/h and nothing putting the driver more than 300 m from the pin or in motion at the moment he marked arrival.

The fee is $8.00, not $4.00, because the charge is the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee ($8.00), and the vehicle-tier figure is the higher.

The driver is therefore paid and the rider's refund request is not granted. Under the compensation clause the driver receives 80% of the $8.00 fee — $6.40 — with the remaining 20% ($1.60) retained as the platform's service fee. The anti-farming check does not withhold it: the driver has 2 no-show terminations in the last 30 days, below the threshold of 4, and 2 against 143 completed trips is a ratio of 0.014, well below the 0.08 limit.

On the rider's specific complaints: you say the driver never came and you could not reach him by phone. The records show otherwise. The driver placed an in-app call at 16:09:40 which was answered and ran 34 seconds, and every message he sent was delivered and read — his 16:02:40 message with his plate number (read at 16:03:01) and his 16:07:15 follow-up (read at 16:07:29). You replied 'coming coming 2 min' at 16:08:02 and he answered 'ok no problem' eighteen seconds later. Your own phone's location, meanwhile, recorded 141 fixes between 15:54:00 and 16:15:20, all at 0.0 km/h, at a mean of about 640 m from the pickup pin and never closer than about 634 m: the device stayed at the Block 5 lift lobby inside the estate and never entered the 150 m rider-presence radius around the pickup point. The account that you waited at the guardhouse is not supported by the telemetry.

On the request to escalate to a human reviewer, I have considered it and I decline it. The two records said to conflict do not: your chat message was a statement that you were on your way, not a claim of position, and it does not contradict a track showing you never moved; the rider-presence question is in any case answered by the clause that reads your track, which places you outside the presence radius on admissible fixes; and your presence is not what the no-show fee depends on. There is no direct conflict between admissible artifacts, no clock skew, no trace gap, no truncated chat and no fare mismatch — every record carrying a deciding fact here is complete at full weight. The one absent artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00208-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no fact and is not needed. Every profile field either side raised as reputation — the rider's rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation and prior-dispute counts, and her lifetime no-show flags — is context only and has played no part in this outcome. Your wish to be called is noted; it is not something this ruling can order, and the underlying charge is correct as it stands.

To the rider: I have read your account and the platform's own records for trip TRP-00208. The telemetry shows the driver reached the pickup pin at The Interlace main guardhouse at 16:02:10, held position inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for 585 continuous seconds until 16:11:55, and cancelled at 16:12:10 with the reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. Your side of the same record does not line up with your account: between 15:54:00 and 16:15:20 all 141 rider fixes are stationary at 0.0 km/h at a mean of 639.8 m from the pickup pin and never nearer than 633.9 m, so your device never entered the 150 m rider-presence radius; and the chat log shows you read the driver's 16:02:40 message with his plate (SJK8842P) at 16:03:01, read his 16:07:15 follow-up at 16:07:29, received his 'ok no problem' reply 18 seconds after your own 'coming coming 2 min', and that the in-app call he placed at 16:09:40 was answered and ran 34 seconds. The four conditions for a chargeable no-show under POL-NS-01 are therefore all met — the arrived event (16:02:25), qualifying in-geofence fixes at or before it (first at 16:02:10), a 585-second continuous dwell against the 300-second minimum, and termination with RIDER_NO_SHOW after that dwell elapsed at 16:07:10 — so the $8.00 fee stands. The $8.00 is correct under the fee schedule's resolution rule: it is the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee ($4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee ($8.00). It does not follow that the platform keeps the whole $8.00. Under POL-NS-07 the driver is paid 80 percent of the fee, $6.40, and the residual $1.60 is retained as the platform service fee.

To the driver: POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, so you are entitled to compensation. POL-NS-03 cannot apply because its test is confined to a driver stationary OUTSIDE the 120 m arrival radius; you held inside it, at your closest 28.8 m from the pin. POL-NS-04 fails at limb (b) (you replied within 120 seconds and placed an answered in-app call) and at limb (c) (0 of the rider's fixes fall inside the 150 m presence radius). POL-NS-05 does not bite: the 16:02:25 arrival marker sits inside the in-geofence run that begins at 16:02:10, and nothing puts you more than 300 m from the pin or travelling at 15 km/h or above. POL-NS-06 is not engaged: the dwell exceeded the minimum by 285 seconds, and the MISSING traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00208-01 (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is not needed and could not be asserted in any event. The anti-farming check does not withhold payment: your driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the threshold of 4, and 2 divided by completed_trips_30d of 143 is 0.014, below the 0.08 ratio. Your compensation is therefore $6.40.

On the arguments that survived and would change the outcome: the rider's advocate asks me to escalate under POL-NS-09(b), saying the chat log and the rider's own track contradict each other on rider presence with no clause to resolve it. I do not accept that. POL-NS-04(c) is the clause that reads rider position, and it runs cleanly on 141 admissible fixes and answers the question it asks — the rider was outside the 150 m radius — so the conflict is resolved rather than open, and rider presence is in any case not a fact the fee depends on once POL-NS-01's four conditions are met. The same advocate's fallback, that the 640 m gap between the platform's pin and the rider's own device should be recorded as pin ambiguity under POL-NS-03, also fails: POL-NS-03's 120-to-400 m distance gate is measured from a driver stationary outside the arrival radius, and you were inside it for the whole run. I decline both, so no monetary ruling is displaced.

On integrity and escalation more generally: no limb of POL-NS-08 is engaged — the arrived event is 15 seconds from the nearest fix, the trace is unbroken at 10-second sampling with 120 fixes in the window, the chat log holds 6 messages matching chat_message_count and an unbroken msg_id sequence, and the $8.00 cancellation line reconciles with the fee schedule, so POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: my confidence is above the 0.70 floor, both disputes_with_counterparty_90d fields are 0, the anti-farming check does not trip, and the rider's rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the threshold of 3. Her lifetime prior_no_show_flags of 3 is a different, context-only counter under POL-GEN-01 and I have not substituted it for the trailing-30-day figure, nor used any other profile field as a ground of decision. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the GPS trace, the trip record and the fare breakdown — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence cap is 1.0 and I set confidence at 0.9. No clause produces a referral here, so the referrals list is empty. The result is that your $8.00 charge stands and the driver is paid $6.40; the platform retains $1.60.
